newsitem.title: USA: Kennedy urges IRA to restore truce.
newsitem.headline: Kennedy urges IRA to restore truce.

text.p: Congressman Joseph Kennedy, joined by Loyalist and Catholic leaders from Northern Ireland, urged the Irish Republican Army on Friday to restore a ceasefire.
Kennedy, a Massachusetts Democrat, also added his voice to those of other Irish-American business and political leaders who have praised the Protestant loyalists for sticking to their truce.
"This is the first time there has been an acknowledgment of the courage and dedication they (loyalist leaders) have shown while the IRA has violated the ceasefire," Kennedy said.
Kennedy said Britain should encourage a ceasefire and be ready for substantive negotiations when it was restored.
Irish Prime Minister John Bruton said earlier on Friday he hoped the IRA was concluding an internal debate to end its policy of violence and agree a new ceasefire.
Bruton, who was speaking in Vienna during a swing through European capitals ahead of an EU summit in Ireland next month, added: "I am not making any predictions as to when this will happen."
